questions.text: In the context of owner and weak entity sets in the ER (Entity-Relationship) data model, which one of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.solution:
A weak entity cannot exist without its owner, so every weak entity must take part in the identifying relationship [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] total participation of the weak entity set.

An owner may have no weak entities (e.g. an employee with no dependents), so the owner's participation is not necessarily total.

Answer: The weak entity set MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: The weak entity set MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship
The owner entity set MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship
Both weak and owner entity sets MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship
Neither weak entity set nor owner entity set MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship

questions.text:
Once the DBMS informs the user that a transaction has been successfully
completed, its effect should persist even if the system crashes before all its changes
are reflected on disk. This property is called
questions.solution:
Once a transaction commits, its changes must survive any later crash (using the log for recovery). This is the Durability property of ACID.

Answer: durability

questions.text:
Consider the following read-write schedule [latex] S [/latex] over three transactions [latex] T_1, T_2 [/latex], and [latex] T_3 [/latex], where the subscripts in the schedule indicate transaction IDs:

[latex] S: r_1(z) ; w_1(z) ; r_2(x) ; r_3(y) ; w_3(y) ; r_2(y) ; w_2(x) ; w_2(y) ; [/latex]

Which of the following transaction schedules is/are conflict equivalent to [latex] S [/latex] ?
questions.solution:
Conflicting pairs (same item, different transactions, at least one write):
- z: only T1 uses it [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T1 has no conflict with anyone.
- x: only T2 uses it.
- y: [latex]r_3(y),w_3(y)[/latex] come before [latex]r_2(y),w_2(y)[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T3 must come before T2.

So any serial order with T3 before T2 is conflict equivalent, and T1 can be anywhere: [latex]T_1T_3T_2,\;T_3T_2T_1,\;T_3T_1T_2[/latex].
[latex]T_1T_2T_3[/latex] puts T2 before T3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not equivalent.

Answer: [latex]T_1T_3T_2[/latex], [latex]T_3T_2T_1[/latex], [latex]T_3T_1T_2[/latex]

questions.text: The symbol [latex] \rightarrow [/latex] indicates functional dependency in the context of a relational database. Which of the following options is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex](X,Y)\rightarrow(Z,W)[/latex] does not give [latex]X\rightarrow(Z,W)[/latex]; Y may be required [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- Decomposition rule: [latex]XY\rightarrow ZW[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] [latex]XY\rightarrow Z[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Pseudo-transitivity: [latex]W\rightarrow Y[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] [latex]XW\rightarrow XY[/latex] (augment by X), and [latex]XY\rightarrow Z[/latex], so [latex]XW\rightarrow Z[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Transitivity: [latex]X\rightarrow Y,\;Y\rightarrow Z[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] [latex]X\rightarrow Z[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Options 2, 3 and 4

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: [latex] ((X, Y) \rightarrow Z \text { and } W \rightarrow Y) \text { implies }(X, W) \rightarrow Z  [/latex]
[latex] (X \rightarrow Y \text { and } Y \rightarrow Z) \text { implies } X \rightarrow Z [/latex]

questions.text:
Consider the following two relations, [latex]R(A, B) [/latex] and [latex]S(A, C) [/latex] :
[latex]\boldsymbol{R} \begin{array}{|c|c|} \hline \boldsymbol{A} & \boldsymbol{B} \\ \hline 10 & 20 \\ \hline 20 & 30 \\ \hline 30 & 40 \\ \hline 30 & 50 \\ \hline 50 & 95 \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]


[latex]\boldsymbol{S} \begin{array}{|c|c|} \hline \boldsymbol{A} & \boldsymbol{C} \\ \hline 10 & 90 \\ \hline 30 & 45 \\ \hline 40 & 80 \\ \hline \end{array} [/latex]
The total number of tuples obtained by evaluating the following expression [latex] \sigma_{B \lt C}\left(R \bowtie_{R . A=S . A} S\right) [/latex] is ____
questions.solution:
Join on [latex]R.A=S.A[/latex]:
- A = 10: (10, 20, 90) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]20 \lt 90[/latex] True
- A = 30: (30, 40, 45) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]40 \lt 45[/latex] True
- A = 30: (30, 50, 45) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]50 \lt 45[/latex] False
(A = 20, 50 in R and A = 40 in S have no match.)

Answer: 2
